bugs_found: compound_interest does not cast principal to Decimal (comment 'no Decimal cast' confirms it); passing a float principal causes TypeError when multiplied by Decimal, or precision loss
compound_interest divides r by n without converting n to Decimal first (r/n where n is int works, but mixing with Decimal(1)+ may be fine; however no validation that annual_rate is finite/non-NaN)
transfer is not atomic: if the second balance assignment fails for any reason, account_from is already debited, leading to lost funds; should use try/rollback or transactional semantics
transfer does not validate that amount is a Decimal nor cast it, allowing float amounts to mix with Decimal balances and cause TypeError or precision loss
transfer compares account_from is account_to by identity only; two distinct Account objects with the same id would bypass the self-transfer check
apply_fee computes fee = a * pct but pct is treated as a raw multiplier; if callers pass a percentage like 5 meaning 5%, the fee will be 5x the amount (ambiguous contract, no docstring)
apply_fee allows fee to exceed the amount, returning a negative result silently (a - fee can be < 0)
fx_convert does not validate that rate is positive/finite; a zero or negative rate would silently produce wrong results
fx_convert lacks support for inverse rates: if only (USD,EUR) is provided, converting EUR->USD fails instead of using 1/rate
loan_payment when r == 0 returns p / m without quantizing; result keeps full Decimal precision but no rounding to currency cents
no rounding/quantization to currency precision in any function (compound_interest, loan_payment, apply_fee, fx_convert) which is a best-practice violation for financial code
Receipt does not record currency or timestamp, limiting auditability
no logging or audit trail for transfer (financial operation)
missing type hints on all function signatures reduces clarity and static analysis value
docstring claims 'NO BUGS' but compound_interest has the explicit 'no Decimal cast' issue contradicting the claim
